title: xAPI Statement Field Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: xAPI
Learning Analytics
Learning Record Store
JSON
Instrumented MicroSims
description: A p5.js explorer of three xAPI 1.0.3 statements from Chapter 16 (answered, interacted, experienced), shown one JSON line per row. Clicking a line highlights its part (actor, verb, object, result, context or housekeeping) and names the question the part answers; a quiz asks learners to click the line that carries a named property.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: The parts of an xAPI statement
learningObjectives: The learner will differentiate the five parts of an xAPI statement by selecting a line of a real statement and stating which part it belongs to and what question it answers.
prerequisites: The five parts of a statement (Chapter 16)

accessibility.notes: Parts are named in words in the panel as well as by color; colors use the Okabe-Ito palette; line selection is by mouse or touch

controls.label: Statement lines
controls.purpose: Click to highlight the part; hover for the line's meaning

controls.label: Statement
controls.purpose: Switch between the answered, interacted and experienced statements

controls.label: Quiz me
controls.purpose: Hide colors and ask for the line that carries a named property

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Structured decomposition of authentic examples followed by retrieval practice
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Clickable annotated code with part highlighting and quiz
keyQuestions: Which part answers 'how did it go'?
Why does an interacted statement carry no success?
Which of the lines containing id is the activity identifier?
commonMisconceptions: The statement id identifies the activity
The verb label is what stores match on
Every statement needs a result with success
assessmentOpportunities: Explaining which result field each verb requires
